articles.title: From ‘Star Wars’ to ‘Alien: How Val Kilmer, Gene Wilder and 3 other late Hollywood stars returned to the screen through AI, CGI and digital effects
articles.summary: Explore how Hollywood is using AI, CGI, and digital effects to resurrect the likenesses of late stars like Val Kilmer and Gene Wilder for modern films. Delve into the ethical debates surrounding consent and the rights of deceased actors as their legacies continue on screen.
articles.body: The use of artificial intelligence (AI), computer-generated imagery (CGI) and digital visual effects has made it possible for filmmakers to bring the likenesses of late actors back to the screen. While some productions have relied on previously unseen footage and digital enhancements, others have recreated an actor’s appearance or voice using advanced technology. These techniques have also sparked debate in Hollywood over consent, creative ethics and the rights of actors after their deaths. From Carrie Fisher’s appearances in the Star Wars franchise to Val Kilmer’s AI-generated role in As Deep as the Grave, here are five late Hollywood stars whose screen legacies have continued through digital recreations.Carrie Fisher in ‘Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker’ and ‘Rogue One: A Star Wars Story’Carrie Fisher, best known for playing Princess Leia in the 'Star Wars' franchise, appeared in films released after her death on December 27, 2016, at the age of 60. For 'Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker' (2019), filmmaker J. J. Abrams used previously unreleased footage of Fisher shot for 'Star Wars: The Force Awakens'. The material was incorporated into the film with the help of visual effects, allowing Fisher’s Leia to remain part of the story. Her daughter, Billie Lourd, also served as a body double for some scenes.According to Industrial Light & Magic (ILM) and The Guardian, Fisher had also appeared digitally in 'Rogue One: A Star Wars Story' (2016), released shortly before her death. Since the film takes place before the events of the original 'Star Wars', the visual effects team recreated a younger version of Leia. Norwegian actor Ingvild Deila served as the on-screen stand-in, with digital effects used to reproduce Fisher’s appearance. The sequence relied on CGI and archival material rather than modern generative AI. The work was part of ILM’s effort to recreate the character’s appearance from the original film.Val Kilmer in ‘As Deep as the Grave’Val Kilmer, who died on April 1, 2025, at the age of 65, is set to appear in 'As Deep as the Grave' through an AI-generated performance. The actor had been cast as Father Fintan, a Catholic priest and Native American spiritualist, but his declining health prevented him from travelling to the set and filming his scenes. According to Variety, writer-director Coerte Voorhees received the cooperation of Kilmer’s estate and his daughter, Mercedes Kilmer, to recreate the actor for the film. The production used photographs from different stages of his life, archival footage and voice material to create the performance.Explaining why he wanted Kilmer for the role, Voorhees told Variety, “He was the actor I wanted to play this role. It was very much designed around him.” He added that the part drew on Kilmer’s Native American heritage and his connection to the American Southwest. The decision has drawn scrutiny amid Hollywood’s wider debate over AI-generated performances. However, Kilmer’s family has supported the project, with his daughter saying that her father viewed emerging technologies as a way to expand storytelling possibilities. The film’s use of AI has brought renewed attention to questions surrounding consent, compensation and the use of an actor’s likeness after death.Peter Cushing in ‘Rogue One: A Star Wars Story’British actor Peter Cushing, who died on August 11, 1994, at the age of 81, returned to the 'Star Wars' universe in 'Rogue One: A Star Wars Story' (2016). Cushing had played Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin in 'Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope' (1977), and the character was brought back for the prequel. Actor Guy Henry performed the role on set, while the visual effects team at Industrial Light & Magic digitally recreated Cushing’s face and likeness. The process combined Henry’s performance with CGI and reference material from Cushing’s earlier work. The filmmakers obtained permission from Cushing’s estate to use his likeness, according to The Guardian.The recreation became a prominent talking point after the film’s release, raising questions about the ethics of digitally reproducing actors who are no longer alive. The visual effects supervisor, John Knoll, defended the decision, telling The Guardian that the work had been done with care and in consultation with the actor’s estate. Cushing’s appearance in Rogue One remains one of Hollywood’s best-known examples of a deceased performer being digitally recreated for a major studio film.Gene Wilder in ‘Wonka’s The Golden Ticket’Gene Wilder, who played Willy Wonka in the 1971 film 'Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory,' returned to the character’s world through his AI-recreated voice in Netflix’s reality competition series 'Wonka’s The Golden Ticket', released in 2026. Wilder died on August 29, 2016, at the age of 83. Rather than recreating his physical appearance, the production used AI technology to reproduce his distinctive voice for the series. According to Netflix’s Tudum, the team sought permission from Wilder’s widow, Karen Boyer, who provided access to old recordings and audiobooks to help recreate his humour, tone and vocal mannerisms.Showrunner Alison Holloway explained why Wilder was the team’s choice, saying, “The only person that could be Wonka is Gene Wilder.” She also expressed gratitude for his widow’s approval of the project. The use of Wilder’s voice offers a different example of posthumous digital recreation, with AI being used for audio rather than a visual performance. It has also added to the ongoing discussion about how a late performer’s voice and identity should be used in new productions.Ian Holm in ‘Alien: Romulus’Ian Holm, the British actor remembered by many audiences as Bilbo Baggins in 'The Lord of the Rings' trilogy, appeared posthumously in 'Alien: Romulus' (2024). Holm died on June 19, 2020, at the age of 88. In the science-fiction film, his likeness was used for Rook, an android resembling Ash, the character he played in the original 'Alien' (1979). Director Fede Álvarez and the visual effects team combined practical effects, CGI and AI-assisted techniques to recreate Holm’s likeness. Actor Daniel Betts contributed to the physical performance, while the production secured permission from Holm’s family and estate.Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Álvarez explained the decision to bring back Holm’s likeness, saying, “It was unfair that the likeness of Ash was never used again.” He added that the team proceeded with the approval of Holm’s widow and children. The recreation proved controversial among some viewers, with criticism directed at both the decision to use a deceased actor’s likeness and the visual effects. The film’s release renewed debate about the boundaries between visual effects, AI and the rights of performers whose images continue to appear on screen after their deaths.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Kristen Bell says she cries weekly over challenges of family life: ‘It’s brutal’
articles.summary: “Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me,” the actress said in a new interview.
articles.body:
Kristen Bell admits she regularly cries over the challenges of family life.

"Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me," the actress said in a new interview.

Bell shares two daughters — Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11 — with husband and fellow actor Dax Shepard.

Just because Kristen Bell is smiling on the red carpet doesn't mean her personal life is always sunshine and rainbows.

The Nobody Wants This star continued her candid streak while discussing the challenges of marriage and raising two kids in the public eye during a recent interview.

"It's hard. Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me," Bell bluntly told Bustle . "It's brutal. I cry weekly."

Bell shares two daughters with her husband of 13 years, Dax Shepard , and is no stranger to speaking honestly about the rocky times that the couple have endured. During the interview, she noted that it feels especially important to open up about those difficulties as a public figure, so other people see their own struggles reflected back at them.

"Oftentimes when you're in that cyclone of puberty, you could think, My kid is the only one doing this," Bell pointed out. "And that is just simply not a fact."

For his part, Shepard praised his wife for her strength in their relationship, sharing that he knew early on that she would be "a force of nature to be reckoned with." He said that he has since been proven correct, joking, "She's not afraid of the gorilla she lives with."

Bell and Shepard have been together since 2007. The couple tied the knot in 2013 after waiting for California to pass same-sex marriage into law, in solidarity with LGBTQ couples who had previously been denied the right to marry. The actors are parents to daughters Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11.

Bell noted that when it comes to booking future gigs, she takes care to put her family first.

"Is this going to pull me away from my kids too much? Will I still be able to be the mom that I want to be? That's really the No. 1, to be honest. There's nothing higher than that," she said. "I would easily let my whole career and all its legacy and notoriety 'disapparate' tomorrow if it meant sacrificing something major in my kids' lives, or not being there."

As for the struggles Bell and Shepard have endured, the couple regularly open up about their past in interviews and on Shepard's Armchair Expert podcast. They have spoken about issues including their brief breakup , which came shortly before they were engaged, and reacting to one another performing intimate scenes with other actors.

Last October, the couple faced backlash for a controversial anniversary post in which Bell recounted Shepard saying to her, "I would never kill you. A lot of men have killed their wives at a certain point. Even though I'm heavily incentivized to kill you, I never would."

The post was met with ire from social media users who labeled the post "tone deaf" and "insensitive" toward victims of domestic violence. Reacting to the pushback just days later, Bell affirmed her deep commitment to her partner of nearly 20 years: "Sometimes it's gonna ebb and sometimes it's gonna flow, but we're not gonna have checks and balances because we're gonna realize it's not me against you, it's us against the world."

articles.title: Blake Shelton 'sick and stunned' as he mourns heartbreaking death – Gwen Stefani reacts
articles.summary: Blake Shelton shared an emotional tribute to John Anderson, revealing he told the country legend he loved him just days before his death. See details
articles.body:
Blake Shelton is "sick" and "stunned." The Grammy-winning singer opened up about his heartbreak on Thursday, October 22 after losing his friend and fellow country singer, JohnAnderson .

The "Boys 'Round Here" singer shared what he is grateful to have said to John during their final meeting, just three days before the country music legend's death.

Following the news that John had died on Wednesday, October 21, aged 71, Blake posted a photograph of them smiling together and reflected on losing both a musical hero and a friend.

"There is too much for me to say about @johnanderson in just a statement. I am sick and I am stunned. But I am a very lucky man," he wrote.

"I got the opportunity to find out that my hero wasn't just the guy I hoped he'd be. He was so much more than that. John was my friend."

The pair had seen each other at the Country Music Hall of Fame's Medallion Ceremony in Nashville on Sunday, October 18. Blake had no idea it would be their last encounter.

"I got to see him last Sunday and I don't even know why but I told him I loved him. That is what fills my heart in this moment," he continued. "My love and prayers go out to John's family. This one really hurts."

Blake's wife and fellow singer Gwen Stefani , 57, reacted to her husband's heartbreak, writing on his post: "Thank you for introducing our family to such a Legend -a one-of-a-kind voice. He will always be part the soundtrack of music that defines who our family. we love u John."

Tim McGraw remembers final evening with John Anderson

Blake was not the only singer remembering a conversation with John at Sunday's ceremony. Tim McGraw , who was among the artists being inducted that evening, also shared a photograph with the country star and recalled the pleasure of spending time together.

"We talked, we laughed, we sang his songs that I loved so much together, just goofing off," Tim wrote on Instagram.

Reba McEntire also joined the tributes, reflecting the affection for John across generations of performers. His distinctive voice had made songs including "Swingin'," "Straight Tequila Night" and "Seminole Wind" enduring country favorites.

John Anderson's family announces his death at 71

John's family said he died peacefully in his sleep. No cause of death has been announced. He is survived by his wife, Jamie , daughters Alexa and Brionna , and their families.

His career began far from the honors he would eventually receive. After leaving Florida for Nashville in 1972, John took construction work while pursuing his musical ambitions.

One of those jobs involved helping build the Grand Ole Opry House, where he worked on the roof before eventually realizing his dream of performing on its stage.

He went on to release more than 20 albums and was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024.

For his family, however, the announcement of his death focused on the man they knew away from the stage. "He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely and made every ordinary moment feel special."

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton claims she received death threats and hate mail after raising Tennessee voting machine concerns, says ‘she would be concerned about me today’; denies being paid by Democrats
articles.summary: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton has claimed she is receiving hate mail and death threats after speaking out about an alleged voting machine issue in
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton has claimed she is receiving hate mail and death threats after speaking out about an alleged voting machine issue in Tennessee, adding that her late sister’s “heart was broken” over the political situation in the United States.Stella, who has been outspoken about her political views on social media, said the backlash would not stop her from raising concerns about human rights and the country’s future. She also claimed that she had faced hostile messages and death threats for years because of her criticism of Donald Trump.“I’ve been getting hate mail and death threats and nasty comments since I started posting on Trump ten years ago,” Stella wrote on Facebook. “I’ve been a human rights activist for decades and that will never change.”In another post, she reflected on her late sister’s concerns about her activism and recalled how Dolly had supported her despite their different approaches to public life.“My big sister’s heart was broken over it but she respected my work. We just worked differently,” Stella wrote. “She would be concerned about me today, when my life was threatened, just like she used to be concerned when I raced cars in celebrity races.”Stella Parton alleges voting machine repeatedly selected Marsha BlackburnThe controversy began after Stella, 77, claimed that a voting machine at the Hermitage branch of the Nashville Public Library repeatedly selected Republican gubernatorial candidate Marsha Blackburn when she tried to cast her ballot for someone else.In a Facebook post on Wednesday, Stella said she had voted during early voting in Nashville the previous week and had to correct her selection three times.“In Tennessee last week at the Hermitage Library where I voted, I had to go back three times and correct my vote because it kept defaulting to Marsha Blackburn,” she wrote. “I would never vote for her for anything.”Stella did not disclose which candidate she intended to vote for. Jerri Green is the Democratic candidate in Tennessee’s gubernatorial race, alongside independent candidates.Urging voters to check their selections carefully, Stella added, “I’m putting this out here because when we vote, we take it seriously but we try not to hold up the long lines. Do it anyway. Don’t let them rig this election.”She later said she was “frightened and frustrated” by the alleged incident and expressed anger over what she described as a lack of accountability in American politics.Stella denies being paid by Democrats to speak about voting machinesAs her posts attracted attention, Stella said some people had accused the Democratic Party of paying her to make claims about the voting equipment. She rejected the allegation, insisting that neither party had ever paid or offered her money.“I have never received or been offered one dime from either party ever,” she wrote. “Everything I post and all the work I do for my state and country is for human rights not any political party.”Stella also criticised political polarisation and said her activism was driven by her commitment to human rights rather than party loyalty. In another post, she expressed hope that Americans would eventually be able to have respectful conversations about the safety and wellbeing of children.She also raised concerns about possible interference by Elon Musk and Russian online accounts. However, there is no credible evidence establishing that Musk or Russian accounts tampered with Tennessee’s election operations.Tennessee election officials respond to voting machine allegationsTennessee election officials have disputed the suggestion that the reported incidents demonstrate deliberate vote manipulation.In a statement to The Tennessean, officials said: “Tennessee’s voting systems are designed with multiple safeguards to help ensure that ballots are recorded consistent with voter intent.”Tennessee Elections Coordinator Mark Goins told WSMV that the reported problems were “not a vote-flipping situation”. He suggested that unintended touches on touchscreen machines could explain some of the issues reported by voters.Chad Gray, election administrator in Williamson County, said officials there had found no discrepancies in their voting equipment. He added that if concerns arose, representatives from each party could examine the devices to ensure they were functioning properly.Other voters claim they experienced similar problemsStella’s Facebook post drew comments from other users who said they had encountered similar touchscreen issues at polling stations.One commenter claimed to have experienced the problem at the Holt Library in Brentwood, adding that they caught the incorrect selection before submitting their ballot.Another said they had to ensure the machine registered their intended choice of Jerri Green before printing the ballot. A third person, who said they had voted at the Hermitage Library, claimed they had to press the button for Green three times before the selection registered.These accounts have not independently established that votes were deliberately changed or that the reported incidents were part of a coordinated effort to influence the election.Dolly Parton kept her political views privateStella’s outspoken political activism contrasts with the public approach of her elder sister, Dolly Parton, who was famously private about her voting preferences and did not publicly disclose which candidates she supported.Dolly, the celebrated country singer-songwriter and philanthropist, died aged 80 on August 25, 2026, following a battle with cancer. She was admired by fans across the political spectrum, while Stella has frequently used social media to speak about human rights and criticise political figures.Stella has maintained that the criticism and threats will not silence her, saying she intends to continue speaking out on issues she believes affect the country and its people.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Former Gosselin Family Housekeeper and Nanny Claims She Saw Kate Abuse Collin and Reported It (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Collin made several claims against his mom in his new memoir, ‘In the Shadow of Eight’
articles.body:
A former house cleaner and part-time nanny for the Gosselin family is speaking out to PEOPLE

The former employee, who worked for the family for six months, alleges strict household rules left the children unable to play freely at home

Now a mother of twins, she hopes her account validates Collin Gosselin's experiences

While Ashley H. was studying for her master's degree in social work in her 20s in 2013, she'd watch TLC's Kate Plus 8 and dream of having a big family of kids someday like matriarch Kate Gosselin's .

Through the years, Kate had given her hope — as she, like Kate, struggled with years of infertility.

"I used to watch the show, like, 'My gosh, this is actually real. You can have infertility issues and you can still have kids,'" Ashley, who prefers to not reveal her last name, recalls to PEOPLE.

At the time, Ashley, now 42, was also working as a nanny. She came across an online posting for a nannying job one day and was surprised to learn it was for Kate and her eight children: twins Mady and Cara and sextuplets Collin, Alexis, Joel, Leah, Aaden and Hannah.

"She didn't say who she was [in the post], just that the nanny could live on the estate, and you could tell she was very, very wealthy," she says. "So, I met her at Starbucks, and she showed up in her sports car."

During their meeting, Ashley realized her class schedule would conflict with the schedule Kate needed a nanny for, so she took a job as her house cleaner and fill-in nanny instead.

When she got to Kate's home in Wernersville, Pa., which was only about 20 minutes from where she studied at Alvernia University, she remembers the "big beautiful family pictures" hanging on the wall.

"I used to think, like, 'Oh, I can't wait to have this someday,'" she says. "Now, I have my nice little house, and I have my canvas pictures of my family up on my walls. But I promised my house would never look unlived-in like Kate's."

Ashley claims that the reality in Kate's home was much different than what was portrayed on TV. She decided to speak out now to back the claims of physical and emotional abuse Collin made against his mom in his memoir, In The Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood .

"She very much outwardly treated Collin different," Ashley says. "She 110 percent abused Collin. It's hard to almost put into words the specific hate that she had towards Collin. You could just feel it. I saw her grab Collin many, many times."

Ashley says Kate had a "house manual" of rules for staff, which included not being able to take pictures of the kids and keeping the family dog out of the house, except for the basement.

"The house was to look unlived-in at all times," she says. "She would have weekly chores, biweekly chores, and they would include having a toothpick and going around the edges of the fridge."

"She wouldn't let the kids do anything," she continues. "There was never toys out. There was never things out. They couldn't live."

Ashley claims the kids were only allowed "either one or two school outfits per week because it would cause too much laundry" and that the interactions between Kate and the kids were "robotic."

"It was not loving," she says. "She very much made it known who was a favorite, who wasn't, who's annoying. Someone would come and pick the dog up for grooming, but she treated her kids basically worse than animals."

One day, Ashley says she opened up a drawer of school supplies and was surprised to find a big, red plastic spoon in it as "everything in the house was always so meticulous."

She asked the kids why the spoon was in there, and "instantly, I'm pretty sure it was Alexis who said, 'Oh, that's the spoon mommy uses when she gets mad.'"

That pushed Ashley to leave the job after only six months.

"I was like, "Oh, okay. I can't work here anymore. This really is as bad as I think it is,'" she says. "That red spoon has haunted me for a long time."

Before leaving, Ashley says she called Children and Youth Services for Berks County on Kate. In his book, Collin claimed a CYS investigation was triggered when he showed up to school in pain after Kate yanked his ear, and he said he later learned multiple reports were made against her.

"She did all the time," Ashley said of Kate's behavior towards Collin. "All the time. She'd rip him right out of his chair in the kitchen."

She says the reason she called CYS was because "I ended up getting sick because I started taking it home with me, because I didn't have my own kids and I didn't understand how somebody could be so nasty, downright evil and nasty to their own kids."

Ashley adds, "I know for a fact that I was not the only one who did that. I want to use this opportunity to not only back Collin that his mom was psychologically abusive to him, not to mention the physical."

By speaking out, Ashley, now a social worker, mental health advocate and mom to twins herself, hopes others will share their own experiences in the Gosselin family home.

"I really hope it will spark people to speak up, even if it's been 15 years later," she says. "I am so incredibly proud of Collin and hope he feels validated."

In 2024, Kate's attorney Richard Puleo told The Sun that he didn't believe that Kate had done anything to "intentionally harm" her son and that "she did what she did to protect herself and her family" from what he called "troubled behavior."

Addressing Collin's book on TikTok, Kate also liked a message from a user who claimed "he" would "regret all of this someday" and alleging that he'd been "encouraged and enabled by other dysfunctional and mentally ill people." They apologized for her having to "relive this over and over" and called the situation "gross."

"Exactly," Kate wrote in the same thread. "I had nothing to do with it, except for consent because it was medically necessary."

Kate and her attorney, Puleo, have not responded to requests for comment on Ashley and Collin's allegations. Children and Youth Services for Berks County declined to comment due to "strict confidentiality laws."

Collin's book In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood is out now wherever books are sold.

articles.title: JK Rowling refuses to back down in essay calling trans activism 'elitist to its core'
articles.summary: Author J.K. Rowling's new essay defended her stance on women's single-sex spaces while calling modern transgender activism "elitist to its core."
articles.body: Author J.K. Rowling reaffirmed her stance on sex and gender issues Wednesday, writing in a new essay that she would not back down from her advocacy despite facing what she described as a relentless "avalanche of death, rape and torture threats." The British author, best known for writing the "Harry Potter" series, published the piece six years after her June 2020 essay sparked widespread debate over transgender rights and women's single-sex spaces. Rowling wrote that her views "haven’t changed" since 2020, but that "the landscape certainly has, and my own involvement in the issue has become practical as well as theoretical, so I thought it was time for an update." JK ROWLING CONFRONTS THE BBC FOR PUSHING 'PROPAGANDA' OVER ITS TRANSGENDER SPORTS HEADLINE Her original essay drew criticism from LGBTQ+ advocacy organizations and transgender rights activists, along with calls to boycott her work. In the new essay, Rowling defended her opposition to policies allowing transgender women into certain female-only spaces, arguing that they undermine protections for women. She also characterized modern transgender activism as "elitist to its core." "It’s true, of course, that trans activism doesn’t impact all women negatively. In fact, the more privileged you are, the less it tends to affect you, and the more it might benefit you. Aside from an avalanche of death, rape and torture threats, it hasn’t noticeably affected my life," Rowling wrote. Rowling has rejected accusations that her views are "anti-trans," maintaining that her advocacy centers on women's safety and privacy. "Should trans people be discriminated against when it comes to housing or employment? Of course not," Rowling wrote. "Should trans people be stripped of their human rights, or denied personal safety? Again: of course not." HBO’S 'HARRY POTTER' GETS A HARD NO FROM 'BLACK MIRROR,' 'LOKI' DIRECTORS OVER JK ROWLING’S TRANS VIEWS Earlier this month, transgender rights activists protested a gala performance of "Harry Potter and the Cursed Child" in London. A demonstrator wore a T-shirt reading, "Rowling money kills," and security personnel eventually removed the protesters from the red carpet. In response to Rowling’s earlier 2020 comments on sex and gender, LGBTQ+ advocacy group GLAAD criticized the author, writing on social media that "JK Rowling continues to align herself with an ideology which willfully distorts facts about gender identity and people who are trans. In 2020, there is no excuse for targeting trans people." Actor Daniel Radcliffe, who starred as Harry Potter in the film adaptations, also publicly criticized Rowling's comments in 2020, issuing a statement through The Trevor Project. "Transgender women are women," Radcliffe wrote. "Any statement to the contrary erases the identity and dignity of transgender people and goes against all advice given by professional health care associations who have far more expertise on this subject matter than either Jo or I." ROYAL FAMILY FACES BACKLASH FROM CRITICS AFTER QUEEN CAMILLA HOSTS JK ROWLING May Mailman, director of the Independent Women's Law Center, told Fox News Digital that she agrees with Rowling's criticism of wealthy supporters of transgender activism, arguing that working-class women are more likely to be affected by policies governing single-sex spaces. "For people in the United States who have real problems to deal with, they need to figure out how they're [going to] put food on the table," Mailman said. "They're not worried about pronouns. They're worried about improving their families and improving themselves. And so, there is this elitism that's like when you run out of problems, you start inventing them." Rowling has also supported the campaign group For Women Scotland, which challenged the interpretation of "woman" under the U.K.'s Equality Act 2010. On April 16, 2025, the U.K. Supreme Court ruled that the terms "woman" and "sex" refer to biological sex for the purposes of the law. The court also affirmed that transgender people remain protected against discrimination under the law's gender reassignment provisions. Mailman welcomed the British court decision but warned that she believes free speech in the country is increasingly under threat. "I think the status of free speech in Great Britain is much more under attack than it is in the U.S.," Mailman said, adding, "I think we should treat it as a warning sign, because I think people look to Britain as where the United States could and often does head." JK ROWLING CALLS OUT THE 'GROTESQUE' BEHAVIOR TOWARDS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS IN SCATHING POST Jeremiah Igunnubole, U.K. legal counsel for Alliance Defending Freedom International, a Christian legal advocacy group, also welcomed Rowling’s essay in a statement to Fox News Digital. "We welcome JK Rowling doubling down on her determination to challenge gender ideology and defend the importance of biological reality. Truth matters, and we should not be afraid to uphold it simply because doing so is controversial," Igunnubole said. articles.title: "We're just a step behind" - what McLaren is trying to solve with its final 2026 upgrades
articles.summary: Slow-corner performance remains a problem for the "knife edge" MCL40, so McLaren has been working towards a revised suspension geometry as well as a differen...
articles.body:
"To get the car to be quick, we just have to try so hard to be perfect, and you cannot be perfect," said Lando Norris after practice for the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix in Austin.

Two mid-season wins for Norris now appear to be a 'purple patch' rather than harbingers of a competitive renaissance for McLaren after a troubled start to the 2026 season. At the US GP it introduced the first elements of what will be the final upgrade package of the year, due to be introduced in stages between this event and the Las Vegas GP.

Although by mid-season McLaren had developed the MCL40 to the point where it was among the fastest cars through quick corners, straightline speed and slow-corner performance have continued to be problematic, as has its nervous demeanour. Development has had to balance the process not just of creating theoretical performance, but also of making the car benign enough for the drivers to tap into that potential.

"It's just on a knife edge on every single corner," said the reigning world champion in Singapore. "You've just got to drive it within an exact percent, and you have to force the car in every single way. You can't let the car do any work. You can't just let the front do the work, or the rear do the work. You have to force the front; you've got to force the rear.

"You've got to drive it in a way that takes so much concentration and so much ability. It's just full-on and mentally draining because of how hard you have to work behind the wheels.

"It's just too difficult and it makes it impossible to put laps together in qualifying, which just shows how good of a job we were able to do when we were getting on pole [in Hungary, the Netherlands and Spain], and how rewarding that felt."

Slow-corner performance isn't just a function of aerodynamics. Although Norris has a more adaptable style than many other drivers, even this requires the car to have a certain set of virtues. He takes a shallower approach to the apex than others, overlapping throttle and brake to a higher degree. His strength is a tremendous feel for where the front tyres pick up lateral grip mid-corner, which he exploits to help rotate the car.

What operates against him is the trend towards running a high degree of anti-squat, anti-dive geometry in the suspension. Although this stabilises the car's aerodynamic platform, it smothers the transmission of 'feel' about the changing state of grip at each axle. Shorn of this, Norris can't trust either end of the car – which is why, last year, his performances picked up dramatically after a slow start when McLaren developed an alternate front suspension geometry suspension for him.

In that context it's no surprise that McLaren has led with a revised front-end geometry for this latest update in Austin, along with reprofiled diffuser furniture. It's understood that the next phase of the upgrade will be applied in Brazil, with more arriving for Las Vegas depending on manufacturing timescales.

The new components McLaren will bring to the car in the coming races were signed off between the Dutch GP in late August and the Italian GP in the first week of September, and have been making their way through the production process. McLaren's design resources have been fully focused on the 2027 car ever since.

Insiders say the team identified a new aerodynamic direction during the April interregnum caused by the cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix. The belief was that it would ultimately lead to a higher performance ceiling than the concept with which the team started the season.

This is a relatively typical occurrence in F1, especially during a new rules cycle. But it is very easy to leap to the conclusion that an upgrade package has somehow been a failure if it doesn't deliver an immediate and significant lap time uplift. From an engineering point of view it is simply establishing a new baseline.

McLaren introduced the first iteration of its new aerodynamic concept in the Azerbaijan GP weekend, centring around a dramatically different sidepod profile, along with heavily revised geometries for the flow conditioners in and around the diffuser, the leading edge of the floor, and the rear suspension fairings. The team was careful to manage expectations, emphasising that it wasn't expecting a major improvement in lap time straight away.

Circumstances then combined to make the new configuration appear, superficially, to be ineffective: Norris was stymied by a fuel injection problem while Oscar Piastri laboured to keep the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar behind him in the early phase of the race, then dropped out of the points after locking up at the second safety car restart. Later the team admitted that at least some of the straightline speed deficit was a consequence of not getting the most out of its Mercedes power unit.

"We will be having some more upgrades coming for the final part of the season, which is the kind of upgrades that follow the foundation set with the upgrades we delivered in Baku," said team principal Andrea Stella after the Singapore round.

"The step in Baku wasn't expected to be big, but it was foundational for some stuff that we will start taking trackside as of Austin and for the coming races. So what's most important for me is that I look forward to seeing our competitiveness from the next race. And hopefully we will be back to being in condition to score podiums and hopefully, once the full package is delivered, to compete for the victory."

McLaren isn't the only team to find itself combatting instability as it tries to add performance to its car. Mercedes went to the extent of running two different car specs in Singapore to try to understand the behaviour of its latest upgrade – but, notably, it has opted for the latest spec in Austin. As Norris explained ahead of the US GP weekend, upgrading an F1 car isn't a predictable and linear process.

"Upgrades are not always just you put them on and things work," he said. "They're not always easy to get the full potential out of. I think we've had a car which has just been still so, so difficult to drive. Yes, we won two races and I had a couple of podium positions, but it was by tiny margins. With a car like that, you'll not be able to do that consistently.

"We need to also improve the car in terms of ease of driving and ease of extracting performance."

articles.title: Julie Andrews Seen in Public for First Time Since Announcing She’s Almost “Completely Retired”
articles.summary: The Oscar winner turned 91 earlier this month.
articles.body:
Julie Andrews was spotted in the Hamptons, New York on October 16.

The actress turned 91 earlier this month.

In August, Andrews revealed that she's almost "completely retired."

Julie Andrews enjoyed a rare outing two months after revealing that she's almost "completely retired." The actress , 91, was photographed in the Hamptons , New York on October 16.

In photos obtained by Page Six , Andrews could be seen wearing a purple coat, a white baseball cap, and sunglasses as got out of her car.

Andrews, who turned 91 on October 1, last walked a red carpet in 2023. More recently, she revealed her decision to step away from onscreen roles. Speaking with The Hollywood Reporter in August, Andrews explained why she decided not to return for the third installment in the Princess Diaries film franchise.

"I think the absolute truth is that I think I'm really past all that now," she told the magazine. "I'm not completely retired, but it's a different kind of work that I do these days—[writing] books, and I do a lot of recording of podcasts and voiceovers. But truly, I don't think I should be a part of it."

Andrews added that it's "still lovely to be working on things," though not "necessarily on camera."

"It isn't that I'm not enthusiastic for it. It's just that I really don't feel I should be part of it now," she continued.

Based on Meg Cabot's books of the same name, the original Princess Diaries movie came out in 2001. Anne Hathaway is set to reprise her role as Mia Thermopolis in the upcoming third installment. In the same THR interview, Andrews was asked about what she thinks the new film will entail.

"Actually don't know," she said. "I think it proceeds from the second Princess Diaries . It moves on, but by now Annie too is a little older than she was when she did it. I'm interested to see what Meg [Cabot] and Annie and everybody comes up with."

articles.body: Vidyarambham on Vijayadasami is significant for artists and anyone pursuing a form of learning. While it marks the beginning of formal education for some, for others, it is an opportunity to start afresh and hone their craft. Celebrities share how they marked the special day.I started with the initiation of new students: Vineeth Actor-dancer Vineeth turned teacher a while ago, and his Vidyarambham begins with initiating new students at his dance school, followed by pujas rooted in his guru’s traditions.“Every year, we have a ritualistic celebration with chilanka puja and Saraswathi puja. After that, we wear the bells and perform guru parampara vandanam, a tradition I learnt from my guru, Sree Padma Subrahmanyam. I follow her pedagogy and the way she conducts the Vijayadashami rituals. We begin with basic adavus and wrap up the celebrations with performances by senior students.“When you start teaching, you realise the value of teaching. You become a student again! I am enjoying that phase now,” he says.My fans did something special for women auto drivers: AnumolActress Anumol celebrated Vijayadashami in a unique way with the support of her fans. She began the day by calling her gurus and seeking their blessings. However, a special initiative by her fan group made the occasion even more meaningful.“A group of fans called Anumol Fangirls, who are like family to me, sponsored auto pujas for 50 women auto drivers in Chennai. They also provided first-aid kits, water bottles, bags, power banks and six months’ worth of sanitary pads. I took part in the initiative to support them and thank them. On a day when we begin learning, doing something like this for women, by women, is heartening,” she says.Anumol makes it a point to meet her teachers wherever she is, depending on who lives nearby. “There are teachers who taught me different things. Whichever city I am in, I try to meet those who are closer to the place,” she says.She also begins the day by writing Om Hari Shree Ganapathaye Namah. “Unlike in our childhood, I now read texts on my phone. Those days when we would accidentally read something on TV and run to our mothers to ask if it was okay to do so during puja are long gone! I have also had the fortune of initiating Vidyarambham for children,” she adds.Every Vidyarambham, I become a student: Rachana NarayanankuttyActress-dancer Rachana Narayanankutty marked the day by introducing her students to a new subject — a global perspective on the Natyasastra.“It is about connecting the Natyasastra with global art forms, and it has a philosophical aspect. Our classes began with that. I had dance sessions for all my students, both online and in person. I still have more classes to take in the afternoon. Later, I will visit my teachers, Thrissur Janardhanan Mash and Gita Padmakumari Teacher, and offer them dakshina,” she says.Her day will not end until she finishes classes with her students based in the US and Canada.For Rachana, Vidyarambham is as much about learning as it is about teaching. “Every Vidyarambham, I become a student. The quality we need as artists is the willingness to remain a student. We can learn a lot from each of our students, and I eagerly look forward to discovering what I can learn from them. Every student is an individual, and each has a different approach to art. There is so much to learn from them,” she says.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Danielle Parton, Dolly Parton’s niece, has officially been selected as the brand ambassador of the estate and is said to carry forward the Partons’ legacy
articles.body: Danielle Parton, Dolly Parton’s niece, has officially been selected as the brand ambassador of the estate and is said to carry forward the Partons’ legacy in the entertainment world. The 50-year-old also shared a video online about the role, expressing how honoured she is for the role.Danielle Parton is named the new brand ambassador of Dolly Parton's estateTaking to her Instagram account, the famed pilot opened up about why and how she landed the opportunity of a lifetime after she was selected as the brand ambassador for Parton’s overall legacy. Describing herself as a “girl boss," Danielle added, “Like so many of you, losing her has changed something for me. It made me think of the stories, values, and lessons that she left behind and the responsibility that our family has to care for them.”She also opened up about how the demise of the country singer was heartbreaking for her and that she refuses to "never try and speak for Dolly." Instead, she was asked to help tell the world the incredible stories of the singer and everyone else.Danielle Parton explains her motivation for taking on this role“I’m not crazy enough to try to fill her shoes. God knows I couldn’t walk on them without killing myself. What I can do is share the woman that I knew. I can tell some of the stories of her, the stories behind the global icon, and support the people carrying forward the work that she cared for and created to make sure what she built continues to bring people joy,” she added. “Yes, Dolly Parton was my aunt, but to me, she will always be Aunt Granny. She loved us deeply and believed in big dreams, and she always encouraged me to find my way in this world. Being a Parton means hard work, big dreams, and never forgetting where you came from. I’m proud to be part of that legacy and to carry it on in my own way. Parton and Danielle had a special bond with each other, which solidified even more at their earlier high school dress.”Dolly passed away at age 80 on August 25 following a “brief battle with cancer.”Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' faces controversy in Tamil Nadu: Film song allegedly replaces National Anthem at Karur theatre
articles.summary: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' has stepped into a controversy after a song was allegedly played instead of India's National Anthem before a screening at a
articles.body: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' has stepped into a controversy after a song was allegedly played instead of India's National Anthem before a screening at a cinema in Karur, Tamil Nadu. The incident reportedly occurred at Ajantha Ellora Cinemas on Coimbatore Road, where the Indian National Flag was displayed on screen before the film began. Videos of the episode have circulated on social media.According to Mid Day, the incident took place while the Nelson Dilipkumar-directed action drama was being screened. The usual pre-show display of the National Flag was reportedly accompanied by a commercial film song rather than 'Jana Gana Mana'.The reported mix-up has prompted questions about how the audio was selected and whether the incident resulted from an error. The reports does not establish why the song was played or whether the theatre has issued an official explanation.Nelson Dilipkumar reunites with Rajinikanth'Jailer 2' is directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and reunites the filmmaker with Rajinikanth after their 2023 film 'Jailer'.'Jailer 2' recorded a decline in domestic collections on Friday, October 23. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 14.50 cr in India net revenue on its ninth day in theatres, with collections coming from 10,484 shows.The figure marked a 15.5% drop from Thursday's India net collection of Rs 17.15 cr. Despite the daily decline, the film's worldwide gross reached Rs 628.05 cr, combining earnings from domestic and international markets. Tamil-language screenings remained a major contributor to the film's domestic earnings on Friday. Sacnilk reported that these shows generated Rs 9.35 cr in India net collections across 4,885 screenings.The Tamil market accounted for 64.5% of the day's domestic net revenue. articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh confirms Delhi concert on October 30; Delhi Police grants permission after security review
articles.summary: Diljit Dosanjh has confirmed his arrival in Delhi for his upcoming concert in the national capital on October 30.
articles.body: Diljit Dosanjh has confirmed his arrival in Delhi for his upcoming concert in the national capital on October 30.Following the controversy surrounding the Delhi leg of his India Aura Tour, Diljit Dosanjh has put an end to speculation about whether he would perform at the concert.The singer shared the video on his Instagram on Friday, saying that he is ready to meet his fans in Delhi. He also took a dig at the buzz and media reports surrounding the controversy."All I wanted to say is: are the reels made? Are the tweets done? Are you guys done? Are the newsroom debates over? Now we meet in Delhi on the 30th. Just throwing debate after debate, posting tweet after tweet. Let me tell you what it is: see you in Delhi. I have arrived," said diljit Dosanjh in Punjabi.While sharing the video, the singer-actor also wrote, "Milde an DELHI. AURA INDIA TOUR 2026."Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming Delhi concert at JLN Stadium has been garnering headlines after Delhi Police initially denied permission for the event in the national capital, citing specific threat-related inputs, multiple security and law-and-order commitments during the ongoing festive season, and other law-and-order concerns on Thursday.However, on Friday, the Delhi Police has granted permission for Diljit's concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on October 30.The decision comes after multiple meetings between Delhi Police officials and the organisers, who presented detailed security plans to address the concerns raised. Following these discussions, permission for Diljit Dosanjh's concert was given.On Friday afternoon, the booking platform also issued a statement confirming that the concert will go ahead as scheduled."It is clarified that reports suggesting that the Diljit Dosanjh AURA India Tour concert in New Delhi on 30 October is being cancelled are inaccurate. Permission for the event had been temporarily withheld, not cancelled, and the two should not be confused. Given the festive season and the heightened caution it calls for, Delhi Police asked the organisers, BookMyShow Live, to put additional safety, traffic and crowd-management measures in place," the statement by BMS read.As per the statement, the booking platform "had a cordial meeting with Delhi Police, presented a detailed plan and have assured Delhi Police of full compliance with all security/traffic requirements. On that basis, permission for the event has been reconsidered and issued. We with Delhi Police are committed to ensure a good experience to the attendees as well as local commuters."Following the Delhi show, the India leg of the tour will move to Indore, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Lucknow. Chandigarh will also be part of the tour, with details of the show to be announced later.Ahmedabad was earlier announced as the first Indian stop of the tour, with Dosanjh set to perform at the Narendra Modi Stadium on November 21. The tour will now cover seven cities over a period of six weeks.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.summary: Reese Witherspoon shares a heartfelt birthday tribute to her son Deacon, reflecting on the fires in Los Angeles at the time of his birth and how they've shaped him into a source of light for others.
articles.body: Actress Reese Witherspoon penned a birthday note for her son Deacon Phillippe as he turned 23, reflecting on the Los Angeles fires that raged around the time of his birth and saying the experience somehow forged him into a person who carries light within and helps others see it in themselves.Witherspoon took to Instagram, where she shared a series of photos of herself with her son, Deacon.The actress took to the caption: "Happy Birthday to my son Deacon, who is turning 23 today ! The year you were born, there was a fire in LA. Raging all around us.""Somehow that fire forged you: You were born into the light, you carry it inside you, and you help us see it in ourselves. I love you so much, so lucky to be your mom. @deaconphillippe," the actress wrote in the caption.Witherspoon met actor Ryan Phillippe at her 21st birthday party in March 1997. They became engaged in December 1998 and married in 1999. They have two children together, daughter Ava Elizabeth Phillippe, born in September 1999, and son Deacon born in October 23.In October 2006, Witherspoon and Phillippe announced their separation.She filed for divorce in November 2006, citing irreconcilable differences. articles.title: I never choose a film thinking, 'This will work with families': Nivin Pauly
articles.summary: With Bethlehem Kudumba Unit (BKU) becoming Malayalam cinema’s biggest blockbuster in terms of footfalls, its success has reinforced something audiences
articles.body: With Bethlehem Kudumba Unit (BKU) becoming Malayalam cinema’s biggest blockbuster in terms of footfalls, its success has reinforced something audiences have come to appreciate about Nivin Pauly: his ability to inhabit characters that feel real. From the repeat-viewing appeal of family dramas to experimenting with different genres, the actor reflects on career choices, the evolving Malayalam film market, social media and the speculation of a reunion with Dulquer Salmaan. Excerpts:What does BKU becoming Malayalam cinema’s biggest blockbuster by footfalls mean to you personally?What has been especially beautiful about BKU is the repeat viewing. Someone watches it with friends and returns with their family. Young people are bringing their parents and grandparents. Milestones like this are wonderful, but they will eventually be surpassed. Malayalam cinema is seeing industry hits more frequently, which is a healthy sign. It means the audience is growing, the market is expanding and bigger achievements are possible. I’m sure the next industry hit is already on its way. For me, the real happiness is that BKU became part of that growth.Age-gap romances can be tricky, as even a small misstep can affect how a relationship is perceived. Did you have any reservations about playing Justin?Every relationship needs to be handled with sensitivity, and this one was no different. What I appreciate about Justin is that he never tries to control Ashley or treats love as ownership. Even when things get difficult, he doesn’t try to separate her from her parents or force her to choose between them and him. They aren’t perfect people, and theirs isn’t a perfect relationship. But there is respect, freedom and a genuine choice to be together. That is what makes their relationship beautiful.Is family-oriented cinema a space where you naturally shine, or have the right films, such as Sarvam Maya and BKU, found you?Family audiences are the hardest to connect with, because you’re not speaking to one age group or one kind of viewer. A teenager, a parent and a grandparent can watch the same film for completely different reasons. So when a film connects across generations, I don’t see a 'family-film space'; I see emotions universal enough to travel. I’ve always been drawn to characters who feel close to life: flawed, funny, vulnerable, sometimes confused. Maybe audiences find it easy to place me in those worlds. But I never choose a film thinking, 'This will work with families'. I choose it because I believe in the character and the emotional truth of the story. With BKU, Girish created a family that doesn’t feel designed for cinema. They’re messy, affectionate, irritating and real. That excited me.You’ve experimented with different kinds of films, some with mixed results. Has that ever made you hesitant?Instinct has guided me throughout my career, starting with my decision to quit my IT job and pursue cinema. Some of my experiments worked, others didn’t, but both gave me clarity. Failure can make you cautious, but if it makes you afraid, you stop growing as an actor. The lesson was never to stop experimenting, but to understand myself better. Now, the question is how much of what people love about me I can retain while still surprising them.Was there a particular experience or decision in the last few years that changed how you look at your career today?Success tells you what works, while failure forces you to understand your choices, mistakes and strengths. Both are necessary. The most important thing is not to give up during a difficult phase. In cinema, one Friday can change everything. But you can’t simply wait for that Friday to arrive. You have to keep working, preparing and improving so you’re ready when it does.You’ve always had an easy connection with humour and everyday characters. Has comedy become more instinctive with experience?A lot of the best humour comes from behaviour... a hesitation, a reaction, an awkward silence or just the way one person looks at another. I really enjoy that kind of comedy, and I genuinely enjoy the process of shooting those scenes. I usually feel very relaxed going into a comedy sequence. A big part of that also comes from my co-actors. Sometimes I enjoy their performances so much that I find it difficult to stop laughing during a take. So, yes, maybe comedy has become more instinctive with experience, but for me, the most important thing is still enjoying the moment and reacting honestly to the people around me.Does making people laugh require a different approach in a family entertainer, or is comedy better when you don’t consciously try to be funny?I prefer not trying too hard to be funny. If the character knows he is delivering a joke, sometimes the humour disappears. But if the character is completely serious and the situation becomes funny for the audience, that is much more enjoyable for me. In a family entertainer especially, humour has to travel across generations. A teenager, a parent and a grandparent may laugh at completely different things in the same scene. So, rather than designing every moment as a punchline, I think it is better to make the situation truthful. Humour usually finds its own way out of that.How do you build chemistry with your co-stars? Your on-screen partnership with Aju Varghese seems to have that chemistry, too...We don’t have to try to create chemistry or build a bond with our co-stars. It happens naturally. We just need to be ourselves. With Aju, it is nice because we are such close friends, and we are close even as families. Even if we don’t have a lot of friends, having a few good friends is still great.Your Tamil projects are at very different ends of the spectrum — an arthouse film like Yezhu Kadal Yezhu Malai and a mass entertainer like Benz. Is that contrast something you consciously look for outside Malayalam cinema?With Ram sir and Yezhu Kadal Yezhu Malai, I entered a completely different cinematic world. The rhythm, philosophy and approach to a character were very different from those in the films I normally do. Benz gives me a completely different kind of energy and scale. I didn’t want to approach the character thinking, ‘Now I have to behave like a villain.’ That can become very external. The more interesting question for me was: why does this man believe he is justified in what he is doing? Most people don’t wake up thinking they are the villain in somebody else’s story. They have their own logic, ego, wounds and ambitions. Finding that internal logic was much more interesting to me than simply trying to look threatening. I enjoy that contrast.How active are you on social media? Do you follow conversations about your films and performances, and do they affect you?Social media is a great way to gauge how people respond to your work. Audiences show their love through messages, edits and posts, and also offer constructive criticism. But it’s not healthy to form an opinion based entirely on social media. Algorithms can keep showing us a particular pattern that may not reflect the wider audience. Personal messages can be more useful because when someone takes the time to explain what moved them or didn’t work, you get a more honest sense of how your work is reaching people.Some Malayalam actors have built a presence across multiple Indian film industries. Do you have similar pan-India ambitions?I’m definitely open to working in different languages. Today, good films can travel far beyond the language in which they are made. For me, what matters most is finding the right character, filmmaker and story.With the OTT boom expanding Malayalam cinema’s reach, do you think the talk of a bigger market is justified?It’s something to be proud of when people speak well of Malayalam cinema. More writers and directors can help us grow further, both in content and commercial success. We also need big films that gross ₹700 crore or ₹1,000 crore, but they must be content-driven. That’s what audiences expect, too. Earlier, even ₹100 crore was a rare milestone. We’ve come a long way, with films grossing ₹300 crore in the last two Onam seasons. Now, the industry is also more connected with distributors outside Kerala. Not every film will work in every region, so we need to understand its core audience and position it accordingly. If a film has potential in a particular market, we should be ready to push it. We did that with BKU and Sarvam Maya. Manjummel Boys, Aavesham and Premalu have also travelled well. It needs strategic planning and a team ready to act when an opportunity arises.We hear your name connected to several projects. What do you have lined up?Dear Students is awaiting release. Multiverse Manmadhan is in the rewriting phase. The same goes for the film with Alphonse Puthren (Premam). Everyone is taking their time to make the scripts better, so I agreed that we should take our time and make decisions as we go. I also have a project with Nashid Famy, the writer of Jaya Jaya Jaya Jaya Hey. It is a fun entertainer, and that is progressing in parallel. I haven’t decided what I will do next after that.On reuniting with Dulquer Salmaan...In Bangalore Days, Dulquer and I played cousins. When we met at an award function after a long gap, his warmth immediately brought back that cousin-like bond. Later, Dulquer distributed my film with Ram sir, Yezhu Kadal Yezhu Malai, in Kerala, and people began speculating about a reunion. We’d both be excited to work together again; it’s about finding the right project. Given the affection and expectations surrounding our reunion, we’d want the film to live up to that excitement.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Deepti Naval shares a 'moment between Nana and her' from 'Yatra'
articles.summary: Deepti Naval shares a nostalgic photo with Nana Patekar from their film 'Yatra' as she pays tribute to the late actor who passed away in 2026. The post highlights their memorable moments together in the film directed by Goutam Ghose.
articles.body: Actor Deepti Naval shared a nostalgic picture with late veteran actor Nana Patekar from their film 'Yatra'.She offered a glimpse into their time working together and shared the picture on her social media account, captioning it as, "A moment between Nana and me.... from Gautam Ghosh's film 'Yatra'."In the picture, Deepti is seen dressed in a traditional blue Nauvari saree with a yellow blouse, seated on the floor beside a traditional stone grinding mill. Nana is seen dressed in a simple off-white outfit with a maroon cloth draped over his shoulder, and is seated beside her.Talking about Yatra', directed by Goutam Ghose, the movie was released in Indian theatres on May 4, 2007, after premiering at the Montreal World Film Festival in 2006.The post shared by Deepti comes as the film industry and fans continue to remember Nana Patekar, who passed away on October 8, 2026, at the age of 75. The veteran actor died following a cardiac arrest in Goa.Deepti had also paid an emotional tribute to the actor in a separate social media post, sharing a picture from their earlier work together. Remembering him fondly, she wrote, "Farewell Nana... You will always be remembered as a true artiste... Rest in peace my dear Nana... I will always miss the child in you!"On the professional front, Deepti, meanwhile, has enjoyed a career spanning many decades. She became popularly recognised with films such as 'Ek Baar Phir', 'Chashme Buddoor', 'Saath Saath', 'Katha', 'Rang Birangi' and 'Kissi Se Na Kehna'.Her other notable films include 'Ankahee', 'Kamla', 'Mirch Masala', 'Main Zinda Hoon' and 'Leela'.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
